item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q014_paper_example_reclassification_pa1492","answer":"In SCOP 1.69, the PA1492 domain from 1t1j and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from 1f8y were assigned to different folds, so SCOP did not encode an evolutionary relationship between them below the broad structural class. In the current SCOPe classification, represented by SIDs d1t1ja_ and d1f8ya_, PA1492 has been merged into the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase-like fold and the two domains are placed in the same superfamily, reflecting probable remote common ancestry. They remain in different families: PA1492-like versus the characterized nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferases. Thus the change is from separate-fold status to superfamily-level homology, not family-level equivalence. It does not by itself justify transferring the 1f8y enzymatic function, substrate specificity, catalytic details, or oligomeric behavior to PA1492; using 1f8y as a modeling template also requires alignment and local structural validation. ASTRAL representative selection is release- and identity-cutoff-dependent and does not change this classification relationship.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
